checks.name: C1 outlines_closed_planar_simple
checks.proves: Every merged plate outline after joinery is a valid face loop: closed, planar in its plate plane, no self-intersection, no zero-length edges, positive area, holes nested inside the outer ring, top and bottom loops paired (same point count) so the loft/BRep between them is a solid.
checks.how: Read plate->features.top / features.bottom ([0] outer, [1..] holes; filled by merge_features called from add_interaction) or plate->polylines[0..1] when features are empty. For each Polyline: (a) closed: get_point(0).distance(last) < 1e-6 (Polyline::is_closed uses Tolerance::ZERO_TOLERANCE=1e-12, too tight for merged points, so compare with 1e-6 explicitly); (b) planar: Plane::from_point_normal(p0, Polyline::newell_normal(points)) and max |plane.signed_distance(p)| < 1e-6, and that plane parallel/coincident with plate->planes[1] (top) or planes[0] (bottom) within 1e-6 (dot of z axes > 1-1e-9); (c) no consecutive duplicates: copy.remove_consecutive_duplicates(1e-6) leaves point_count unchanged; (d) area() > 1e-6 mm2; (e) simple: O(n^2) over non-adjacent segment pairs with Intersection::line_line_parameters(seg_i, seg_j, t0, t1, 0.0, true, true) and point distance < 1e-6 -> fail (kernel has no is_simple, see gaps); (f) holes inside outer: Polyline::boolean_op(outer, hole, plane, 0) returns one ring whose area == hole.area() within 1e-6 relative; (g) features.top.size()==features.bottom.size() and top[i].point_count()==bottom[i].point_count() (Mesh::loft/brep_between_loops pair loops index-wise).
checks.applies_to: All plate families: ss_e_ip, ss_e_op, ss_e_r, ts_e_p, cr_c_ip, side_removal, side_removal_ss_e_r_1_port, custom variants; tt_e_p only when the merge emits hole loops (otherwise outlines equal the stock). Not beams.

checks.name: C2 solids_closed_valid
checks.proves: Both members' model solids and the joint's own solid are closed, single, positive-volume bodies as mesh and as exact BRep, and the two representations agree.
checks.how: For a, b and the joint: Mesh m = e->model_geometry_mesh(): m.number_of_faces()>0, m.is_closed(), m.naked_edges().empty(), compute_volume(m) > 0 (wood's compute_volume handles holed caps; Mesh::volume fans the outer ring and counts holes as solid, do not use it on cut plates). BRep br = e->model_geometry_brep(): br.is_valid(), br.is_solid(), br.solid_count()==1, |br.volume() - compute_volume(m)| <= 1e-9*V for planar-only solids and <= 1e-3*V when the BRep has rational (cylindrical) surfaces (count NurbsSurface::is_rational over br.m_surfaces, as count_bores does). Joint: joint->element_geometry_mesh().is_closed() and element_geometry_brep().is_valid()&&is_solid() (already asserted for one joint in joint_elements.cpp:226-227). Also the pieces: for each Mesh piece = Mesh::loft({body[0]},{body[1]},true) over JointPlate::bodies() (protected: expose or recompute from connections[i].male_outlines/female_outlines pairs with >=3 points and equal counts): piece.is_closed() and compute_volume(piece) > 0.
checks.applies_to: All families, plate and beam (JointBeam feature joints: j->element_geometry_mesh(); connectors: part_brep(i), children()).

checks.name: C3 no_interpenetration
checks.proves: After the joint the two members do not overlap in space (the joint actually separates them; for cr_c_ip the pre-joint crossing overlap is removed).
checks.how: Mesh overlap = solid_boolean(a->model_geometry_mesh(), b->model_geometry_mesh(), SolidOperation::intersect, 1e-7); pass when overlap.number_of_faces()==0 or compute_volume(overlap) < 1e-6 * min(V_a, V_b) (floor_elements uses absolute 1e-2 mm3; relative is safer across plate sizes). For cr_c_ip additionally assert the pre-joint overlap solid_boolean(a->element_geometry_mesh(), b->element_geometry_mesh(), intersect) has volume > 0 so the check is not vacuous. Members must stay in their joined position: the fixture must NOT call place()/Xform to draw them apart as the element examples do. Also pieces vs. host: each male piece intersect model_b volume ~0 is implied by C3; each female piece (the hole volume) must not intersect model_b (solid_boolean(piece, model_b, intersect) volume < 1e-6*V_piece).
checks.applies_to: All families; cr_c_ip is the family where the pre-joint overlap is non-zero; ss_e_ip/ss_e_op/ts_e_p/tt_e_p pre-joint overlap is already ~0 so the check guards regressions where fingers protrude into the neighbour.
checks.refs: wood/src/joinery_solver/wood_elements/wood_element_geometry.h:11-13; wood/src/joinery_solver/wood_algorithms/wood_solid_boolean.cpp:394-424; wood/tests/floor_elements.cpp:985-1007; wood/examples/elements/element_joint_plate_ss_e_ip.cpp (right->place(...) after joining; do not copy)

checks.name: C4 material_conservation
checks.proves: Joinery only redistributes and removes material: nothing is created outside the original stock of the pair, and nothing is lost except the holes of pins.
checks.how: Mesh stock = solid_boolean(a->element_geometry_mesh(), b->element_geometry_mesh(), SolidOperation::add, 1e-7) (pairwise union; for cr_c_ip the stock union has the crossing merged); Mesh after = solid_boolean(model_a, model_b, add). (1) outside = solid_boolean(after, stock, subtract): faces==0 or compute_volume(outside) < 1e-6*V(stock). (2) lost = V(stock) - V(after) >= -1e-9*V(stock); for families without drills lost <= 1e-6*V(stock) for in-plane/out-of-plane finger joints where male fingers fill female notches exactly (ss_e_ip_1 is symmetric male/female), otherwise lost == V(expected pockets) (ts_e_p: 0 when tenon fills mortise; cr_c_ip: 0; side_removal: lost == V(elem_b) - V(model_b) > 0 by design). For tt_e_p: lost == sum over drill axes of pi*r^2*(length inside a + inside b) within 1e-2 relative for the polygonal drill mesh (circle_segments(radius, chord_tolerance)), or compare after.volume via BRep within 1e-3. Note on volumes: V(model_a)+V(model_b) == V(after) when C3 holds, so also assert |V_a + V_b - V(after)| < 1e-9*V(after).
checks.applies_to: All families; the exact 'lost' expectation differs per family (0 for finger/tenon/cross families, hole volume for tt_e_p, pocket volume for side_removal/ss_e_r mill types).
checks.refs: wood/src/joinery_solver/wood_elements/wood_element_geometry.h:11-16,27-28; wood/src/joinery_solver/wood_algorithms/wood_solid_boolean.cpp:394-440 (largest_piece 362-389 applies only to solid_difference, so use solid_boolean for the oracle to avoid dropping pieces); wood/src/joinery_solver/wood_interaction/wood_interaction_feature/wood_interaction_feature_plate_joints/ss_e_ip_1.h:1,53-62; wood/tests/floor_elements.cpp:1002-1004,218-239

checks.name: C5 pieces_inside_contact_zone
checks.proves: Every solid piece a joint makes (tenon, finger, slot volume, notch) lies inside the joint volume the contact defines, i.e. the joint cuts where the members meet and nowhere else.
checks.how: Zone = convex hull of the points of connection.joint_volumes[0..3] (the oriented unit box mapped by joint_orient_to_connection_area) grown by settings.joint_volume_extension (joint_volume_extension(settings.joint_volume_extension, joint_type)) and by 1e-6: Mesh hull = ConvexHull::hull_3d(points) (fallback: use the four rectangles' AABB inflated when hull degenerates for coplanar input). For every piece from JointPlate bodies: outside = solid_boolean(piece, hull, subtract) -> faces==0 or compute_volume(outside) < 1e-6*V(piece). Also every drill axis endpoint of JointPlate::drill_axes() must lie within the inflated AABB of the contact polygon extruded by both thicknesses. Cheaper variant without booleans: every piece vertex inside hull via Intersection::ray_mesh_bvh parity (needs a point-in-mesh helper, see gaps).
checks.applies_to: ss_e_ip, ss_e_op, ss_e_r, ts_e_p, cr_c_ip, side_removal (pieces); tt_e_p (drill axes only). Beam joints: JointBeam::feature.volumes rectangles for from_contact; connector parts for wedge/tie/rectangle_plate.

checks.name: C6 male_fits_female
checks.proves: The tenon/finger of the male occupies exactly the volume the female lost (no gap, no interference), and the swap is symmetric for symmetric designs.
checks.how: taken_b = compute_volume(b->element_geometry_mesh()) - compute_volume(b->model_geometry_mesh()); filled_by_a = compute_volume(solid_boolean(a->model_geometry_mesh(), b->element_geometry_mesh(), intersect)) i.e. what a now occupies inside b's original stock; assert |taken_b - filled_by_a| <= 1e-6*max(taken_b, 1e-9) + (for tt_e_p) the hole volume in b. Symmetric for a. For cr_c_ip (both halves lapped) also taken_a == taken_b (floor_elements precedent). For ts_e_p the mortise is a through hole of the base: taken_base == V(tenon pieces) where tenon pieces = male bodies clipped to the base's slab: solid_boolean(piece, base->element_geometry_mesh(), intersect). For side_removal there is no male counterpart: assert filled_by_a == 0 and taken_b > 0.
checks.applies_to: ss_e_ip_*, ss_e_op_*, ss_e_r_*, ts_e_p_*, cr_c_ip_* (strict); side_removal (one-sided); tt_e_p (hole-adjusted); JointBeam from_contact (cross/side-to-end volumes).

checks.name: C7 drill_holes_count_radius_depth
checks.proves: Each pin axis the joint declares is drilled in both members with the pin radius, through the right depth, and the exact BRep carries one cylinder per hole.
checks.how: axes = joint->drill_axes() (JointPlate: FabricationType::drill 2-point outlines, de-duplicated; Joint/JointBeam: drill_lines); n = axes.size() > 0 for tt_e_p (tt_e_p_2 expects `count` points on the circle, tt_e_p_3/4/5 spacing-based: assert n >= 1 and n <= area/spacing^2 + perimeter/spacing + 4; do not hard-code counts unverified). Per member: (a) hosted drill features: count of ElementFeature with feature_type=='drill' and guid starting with joint->guid()+'/' (drills_of pattern) == number of inside stretches of axes in that member; each feature has two closed circles whose points are at distance radius (+-1e-9) from the axis (circles come from Polyline::from_sides(DRILL_SIDES, radius, true)); (b) depth: Intersection::ray_mesh_bvh(axis, member->element_geometry_mesh(), 1e-9, true) gives 2 hits whose distance == member thickness (+-1e-6) for a through hole; (c) exact: count rational surfaces in member->model_geometry_brep() == stretches in that member, brep.is_solid(), |brep.volume() - compute_volume(model mesh)| <= 1e-3*V; (d) mesh: V(elem) - V(model) == pi r^2 * depth within 1e-2 relative (polygon chord error). Unverified: whether the JointPlate add_interaction path (host_feature + merge_features, no host_drills/host_solid_feature) ever drills the plate solids for tt_e_p; if (a)/(c) report 0 the gap is in the port, not the oracle.
checks.applies_to: tt_e_p_0..5; JointBeam::centred_pins / headed_pins (pre_drill), wedge, rectangle_plate, tie; Joint::drill; Pin children.

checks.name: C8 contact_preserved_outside_joint
checks.proves: The joint does not destroy the bearing contact: the members still meet on the original contact plane with the same overlap region (minus the joint pieces), and the contact polygon the solver computed is consistent with the faces it names.
checks.how: Before joining: contact->polygon.is_closed(), area > settings.clipper_area, planar within 1e-6, and boolean_op(a->polylines[face_a], polygon, plane_a, 0) area == polygon area (polygon subset of face_a); same for face_b with the plate's plane. After joining: loops_a = a->model_geometry_mesh().section_by_plane(plane offset by +1e-3 along the contact normal into a) and loops_b likewise into b; sum of areas of closed loops of a and b equal within 1e-6 relative, and each >= polygon.area() - sum(piece section areas) (fingers/tenons change the section only inside the joint volume). Alternative exact statement for ts_e_p: the base's top face area after == area before - mortise hole area (hole areas from features.top[1..]).
checks.applies_to: Face-contact families ss_e_ip, ss_e_op, ss_e_r, ts_e_p, tt_e_p, side_removal; cr_c_ip uses the cross contact polygon (InteractionContactCross) instead.

checks.name: C9 parameters_change_what_they_say
checks.proves: divisions and shift drive the geometry as documented: piece counts follow the division formula, shift moves vertices without changing volume for symmetric designs, and defaults equal explicit defaults.
checks.how: (a) counts: ts_e_p_3(div): female plate features.top holes == div/4 (div clamped to [8,100] and rounded down to a multiple of 4), male pieces (bodies with >=3 points) == 2*(div/4) (top+bottom pair per tenon; verify the exact factor once from bodies() and freeze); ss_e_ip_1(div): merged outline point count of each plate == 5 + (2*div_even + 2) - 2 where div_even = even(max(2,min(100,div))) (freeze the constant from one run, then assert monotonic growth with div); ss_e_r_2/3(div): pieces == 2*div*2 faces. (b) shift: for ss_e_ip_1 and ts_e_p_3 at shift 0.0, 0.5, 1.0 with the same div: V(model_a)+V(model_b) equal within 1e-9 relative and the set of merged outline vertices differs (max point displacement > 1e-3) between shift 0 and 1. (c) defaults: JointPlate::ss_e_ip_1() and ss_e_ip_1(8, 0.5) give identical merged outlines (point-wise 1e-9) and parameters.pb_dumps() equal. (d) same variant on a and on the flipped contact order (joint oriented on contact->flipped()) gives mirrored but volume-equal results within 1e-9.
checks.applies_to: ss_e_ip_1/2/5, ss_e_op_1/2/4/5/17, ts_e_p_2/3/5, ss_e_r_2/3, cr_c_ip_1, tt_e_p_2/3/4/5 (count/spacing).

checks.name: C10 invariance_round_trip_and_rigid_motion
checks.proves: The geometry is a function of the inputs only: protobuf round trip and a rigid motion of the whole pair reproduce the same volumes and outlines; a mirror is refused.
checks.how: restored = WoodSession::pb_loads(scene.pb_dumps()); for each plate: compute_volume(model) equal within 1e-9 relative, features.top/bottom point-wise equal within 1e-9 (floor_elements round-trip precedent). Rigid motion: build the same fixture with every input point transformed by Xform::translation(1234,-567,89) composed with a rotation about z by 37 deg (Xform API in kernel); model volumes equal within 1e-9 relative, merged outlines equal after transforming back within 1e-6. Mirror: Plate::transformed(mirror xform) returns nullptr (is_mirror) -> assert nullptr.

checks.name: C11 golden_outline_snapshot
checks.proves: Any change in a variant's merged outlines (the picture) is detected numerically and must be acknowledged by regenerating the golden file.
checks.how: After the checks, io::write_parity_dumps(scene, tests/golden/joint_library/<variant_id>) writes <id>_meta.txt (per plate: polyline count and point counts) and <id>_coords.txt (per plate, per polyline, xyz). Compare to the committed files: meta must match exactly; coords within 1e-6 absolute (mm) per coordinate. With env WOOD_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 the files are rewritten instead of compared. Path from a compile definition WOOD_SOURCE_DIR as rust_elements does. write_parity_dumps dumps plates only; beam joints and JointPlate bodies/drill axes need an extension (see gaps) or an in-test dump of bodies() loops and drill_axes() in the same format.
checks.applies_to: All plate variants in the loop (and datasets in C12 if desired, one file per dataset).

checks.name: C12 datasets_pairwise_oracle
checks.proves: The solver's own detection + library on the real datasets produces valid, non-interpenetrating, material-conserving members for every adjacent pair, not just a joint count.
checks.how: For each data/*.yml (list from wood_datasets.h, same loader as joint_elements.cpp:339-363: config::reset_defaults(); WoodSession::yaml_load(name); compute_face_contacts() or compute_cross_contacts(); compute_features(search type)), then for every plate run C1 and C2, for every adjacency pair (scene.adjacency when present else all pairs with a plate-joint edge in scene.graph) run C3 with tolerance 1e-6*min volume, and globally sum(model volumes) <= sum(element volumes)*(1+1e-9) and union containment C4(1) per pair. Budget: run under `timeout 600` like CI's main_all_datasets; skip vidy_full/annen_grid_full_arch unless WOOD_FULL_DATASETS=1 (runtime unverified). 2024 out.xml comparison: not feasible as a per-dataset reference (see datasets); instead freeze C11 goldens per dataset from the current port after a visual sign-off.
checks.applies_to: All plate datasets (ss_e_ip, ss_e_op, ts_e_p, tt_e_p, cross, annen, vidy); beam datasets (phanomema_node, beams in Settings::beams) with C2/C3 only.

No enable_testing()/add_test()/ctest anywhere in wood/CMakeLists.txt; session/session_cpp/CMakeLists.txt also has none, its kernel tests are one mini_test runner `point_minitest` (session/session_cpp/CMakeLists.txt:412; MINI_TEST macro session/session_cpp/src/mini_test.h:56-58) driven by session/bash/minitest.sh / quicktest.sh. datasets:
Current: wood/data/*.obj with matching *.yml (settings) and sidecars *_adjacency.txt, *_insertion_vectors.txt, *_joints_types.txt, *_three_valence.txt for annen_* and vidy_*; loaded by WoodSession::yaml_load(name) (wood/src/joinery_solver/wood_session.h:85) after config::reset_defaults() (tests/joint_elements.cpp:177-178,340); the names run as tests are listed in wood/src/joinery_solver/wood_datasets.h:9-80 (hexbox_and_corner, vidy_corner, vidy_one_layer, vidy_one_axis_two_layers, vidy_full, inplane_butterflies, inplane_hexshell, inplane_differentdirections, vidy_folding, outofplane_box, outofplane_box_miter, outofplane_tetra/dodecahedron/icosahedron/octahedron, simple_corners, simple_corners_combined, simple_corners_diff_lengths, inplane_hilti, top_to_top_pairs, hexboxes, hex_block_rossiniere, top_to_side_snap_fit, top_to_side_box, plus cross_* and annen_* in the file beyond line 80, not read) and executed by build/main_all_datasets (wood/CMakeLists.txt:251, CI wood-test.yml:64-66). data/output/ holds pb output, data/face_to_face_detection and data/templates exist (contents not read). Families covered by datasets: ss_e_ip (inplane_*), ss_e_op (outofplane_*, vidy_folding), ts_e_p (top_to_side_*), tt_e_p (top_to_top_pairs, hexboxes), cross (cross_*), rotated/three-valence (vidy_*), annen (annen_*), beams (phanomema_node).
2024 (351933c): cmake/src/wood/dataset/ holds ~40 input xml files type_plates_name_*.xml (+ type_beams_name_phanomema_node.xml, in_beam_node_0.xml) with reference screenshots *.png, and exactly ONE output file out.xml (18431 bytes: 12 <polyline_group>, 24 <polyline>, i.e. 12 plates x top/bottom outlines of 9 points, first points around x 24/-14/-74/-120, y 955..1045, z 30.04 and 147.04) plus 22_11_22_backup/out.xml (210900 bytes, 42 groups). out.xml is the last run's output: every test writes to wood::GLOBALS::DATA_SET_OUTPUT_FILE = DATA_SET_INPUT_FOLDER + "out.xml" (351933c:cmake/src/wood/include/wood_globals.cpp:21; wood_test.cpp:250-251) with OUTPUT_GEOMETRY_TYPE default 4 (wood_globals.cpp:32). Which dataset produced either snapshot is not recorded (unverified; coordinates match no obviously-named small dataset; several current .obj files contain the value 1045). Feasibility of 'match out.xml within tolerance': low. It would require identifying the dataset by plate count/coordinates, re-running it in the port with the same global parameters (JOINTS_PARAMETERS_AND_TYPES, scale, search_type), then matching 12 plates' merged outlines modulo plate order, outline start vertex and winding, at ~1e-3 mm. It covers at most two datasets and only merged plate outlines (no holes-as-solids, no drills). Recommendation: do not build the oracle on it; keep it as a one-off manual comparison, and freeze new goldens from the port with write_parity_dumps (wood/src/joinery_solver/wood_io.cpp:143-167) after visual sign-off.
Port-vs-2024 vocabulary differences worth a one-time check (unverified whether translated anywhere): old cut_type enum order nothing=0, edge_insertion=1, hole=2, insert_between_multiple_edges=3, ... drill, drill_50, drill_10 (351933c:cmake/src/wood/include/wood_cut.h:18-42) vs current FabricationType nothing=0, hole=1, edge_insertion=2, insert_between_multiple_edges=3, ..., drill=15 and no drill_50/drill_10 (wood/src/joinery_solver/wood_interaction/wood_interaction_feature/wood_interaction_feature_fabrication_type.h:6-23). Old joint fields m/f + m_boolean_type/f_boolean_type, unit_scale, unit_scale_distance, shift, divisions, scale, linked_joints, linked_joints_seq (351933c:cmake/src/wood/include/wood_joint.h:64-69,85-102,245-247) map to InteractionFeaturePlate fields (wood_interaction_feature_plate.h:26-39). Old library has ss_e_op_6, ts_e_p_4, tt_e_p_custom (351933c:cmake/src/wood/include/wood_joint_lib.h:294,397,583) which the current header does not expose (wood_element_joint_plate.h:64-170); current adds ss_e_op_17, ss_e_op_tutorial, ts_e_p_1, ss_e_r_1 factories.
test_design:
File: wood/tests/joint_library.cpp, one executable `joint_library`, house style (explicit types, no lambdas, short functions, section banners, `check(bool, message)` throwing as in tests/brep_drill.cpp:9-14). Includes: wood_session.h, wood_element_geometry.h (solid_boolean, compute_volume, cut_mesh), wood_brep_drill.h (optional), wood_io.h (write_parity_dumps), convex_hull.h, <filesystem>, <fstream>.

Constants (top of file): CLOSE = 1e-6 mm (outline closure/duplicates), PLANAR = 1e-6 mm, VOLUME_REL = 1e-9 (planar solids, round trips), ROUND_REL = 1e-3 (BRep with cylinders vs mesh), HOLE_REL = 1e-2 (polygonal drill mesh vs pi r^2 L), ZERO_REL = 1e-6 (overlap/outside volumes relative to the smaller member), MANIFOLD_TOL = 1e-7 (InteractionFeatureSolid::tolerance default).

Fixtures (one function each, returning the two plates added to a fresh WoodSession and the contact; the pair stays joined, never place()d apart):
- pair_in_plane(scene): Plate::from_rectangle({0,0,0},{1,0,0},{0,1,0},300,400,40,"left") and ({300,0,0},...,"right"); contact = scene.compute_face_contact(left,right); expect ContactType::side_side; serves ss_e_ip_* (contact_type 12), side_removal (family 11 by contact), custom ss_e_ip. [from examples/elements/element_joint_plate_ss_e_ip.cpp]
- pair_out_of_plane(scene): floor Plate(bottom {0,0,0},{300,0,0},{300,400,0},{0,400,0}; top at z=40 with x 260) and wall Plate(bottom x=300 plane 0..300 high; top x=260 from z=40) i.e. the mitred corner; contact side_side; serves ss_e_op_* (11), side_removal_ss_e_r_1_port and ss_e_r_* need a rotated fixture (below). Per-variant loop (function run_variant(id) -> std::vector<std::string> failures): fresh WoodSession scene(id); pick the fixture by the family prefix; joint = make_variant(id); joint->orient(contact, {a, b}) (face) or orient(cross_contact, {a, b}); scene.add(joint); scene.add_interaction(joint, first_target, joint->interaction(0)); scene.add_interaction(joint, second_target, joint->interaction(1)); then C1 (outlines), C2 (solids, BRep agreement), C3 (overlap), C4 (outside/lost), C5 (pieces in zone), C6 (fit), C7 (drills, tt_e_p and beam connectors), C8 (contact preserved), C9 (only for the parameter sub-table: it reruns the same fixture at shift 0/0.5/1 and compares), C10 (pb round trip + rigid motion rebuild), C11 (golden). Each check appends a message instead of throwing so one run reports every failing variant; main() collects all failures, prints a table `variant | V_a | V_b | lost | pieces | drills | ms` to stdout, prints failures to stderr and throws once at the end (non-zero exit). Expected runtime: a few lofts and 4-6 Manifold booleans per variant, well under a minute total (unverified).
